question: What breaks if we switch off sso-legacy?
summary: Switching off sso-legacy would stop invoice-render and reports-legacy outright and slow down billing-api, onboarding and web-console, touching 16 customers. The risk is high (score 100) and it cannot be auto-approved. The main link (invoice-render relying on sso-legacy) is not written down anywhere, so it is easy to miss.

claims.text: Switching off sso-legacy directly stops invoice-render and reports-legacy.
claims.reason: the records show each of these

check.cypher:
breadth-first over DEPENDS_ON from every :Retired service; each witness path re-runs as:
UNWIND $edges AS e
MATCH (a)-[r:DEPENDS_ON {uid: e}]->(b)
RETURN a.uid AS from_uid, a.name AS from_name, b.uid AS to_uid, b.name AS to_name, r.uid AS uid, r.kind AS kind,
       r.declared AS declared

claims.text: Billing-api, onboarding and web-console would slow down or partly fail, through invoice-render.
claims.reason: the records show each of these

check.cypher:
breadth-first over DEPENDS_ON from every :Retired service; each witness path re-runs as:
UNWIND $edges AS e
MATCH (a)-[r:DEPENDS_ON {uid: e}]->(b)
RETURN a.uid AS from_uid, a.name AS from_name, b.uid AS to_uid, b.name AS to_name, r.uid AS uid, r.kind AS kind,
       r.declared AS declared

claims.text: The dependency of invoice-render on sso-legacy is not declared; it only appears in the records as an undeclared link, so it is the path that takes down billing-api, onboarding and web-console.
claims.reason: The rows show invoice-render relying on sso-legacy at one hop, but they do not say the dependency is undeclared, and they show billing-api, onboarding and web-console being degraded rather than taken down. They also do not establish invoice-render as the sole path causing those effects.

claims.text: Sixteen customers would notice: five enterprise (Helio Robotics, Mosaic Health, Northgate Retail, Pinecrest Bank, Vireo Mobility), seven growth (Brightline Games, Copperleaf Energy, Fernway, Glasswing Security, Quillsoft, Sable Analytics, Tandem Logistics) and four starter (Juniper Learning, Kiln Studio, Larkspur Media, Otterly).
claims.reason: the what-if's customer list shows exactly this

check.cypher:
MATCH (s:Service) WHERE s.uid IN $services
OPTIONAL MATCH (c1:Customer)-[:USES]->(s)
OPTIONAL MATCH (c2:Customer)<-[:RAISED_BY]-(k:Ticket)-[:ABOUT]->(s) WHERE k.at >= $since
WITH s, collect(DISTINCT c1) AS users, collect(DISTINCT {c: c2, key: k.key}) AS raised
UNWIND users + [x IN raised WHERE x.c IS NOT NULL | x.c] AS c
WITH s, c, users, [x IN raised WHERE x.c = c | x.key] AS tickets
RETURN DISTINCT c.uid AS uid, c.name AS customer, c.tier AS tier, s.uid AS service_uid, s.name AS service, tickets,
       c IN users AS uses

claims.text: Four teams must approve: Billing, Console, Data and Platform.

check.cypher: what-if u1 against the company it was copied from: the teams that own or run something the change touches

claims.text: Risk of the switch-off is high, score 100, and it is not auto-approved.

check.cypher:
MATCH (u:Universe {uid: $u})
OPTIONAL MATCH (u)-[:SCORED]->(t:RiskTerm)
WITH u, collect(t) AS terms
RETURN CASE WHEN reduce(s = 0.0, t IN terms | s + t.points) > 100 THEN 100
            ELSE toInteger(round(reduce(s = 0.0, t IN terms | s + t.points))) END AS risk_score,
       [t IN terms | {kind: t.kind, subject: t.subject, points: t.points}] AS terms

claims.text: No system would be left without anyone who knows it.

check.cypher: what-if u1 against the company it was copied from: services someone knew before and nobody knows after (no incoming KNOWS)

claims.text: Invoice-render is known only by Ines Okafor.

check.cypher:
MATCH (s:Service {uid: $s})
OPTIONAL MATCH (p:Person)-[:KNOWS]->(s)
RETURN count(p) AS knowers, collect(p.name) AS people, collect(p.uid) AS uids

claims.text: Nobody is recorded as knowing reports-legacy.

check.cypher:
MATCH (s:Service {uid: $s})
OPTIONAL MATCH (p:Person)-[:KNOWS]->(s)
RETURN count(p) AS knowers, collect(p.name) AS people, collect(p.uid) AS uids
